ad15_lobbying.topic: Federal lobbying by industry, campaign finance, influence evidence, revolving door, Direct File case

claims.text: Statista: total lobbying spending $4.27bn in 2023 and $4.44bn in 2024
LegiStorm: $5.24bn in 2025, up $768m from 2024 (about 17%); outside firms $2.76bn (+25.3%), in-house $2.46bn (+8.5%); 15,592 clients vs 13,910

NBC/OpenSecrets: federal lobbying a record $4.2bn in 2023; health sector over $739m, the most of any sector; Chamber of Commerce $69m and NAR $52m in 2023; NAR $82m and Chamber $81m in 2022; state lobbying $1.4bn in 2023

OpenSecrets Q2 2025: pharmaceuticals and health products $105.4m in Q2, $226.8m in first half 2025; pharma outspent every industry in all but one quarter since 2010; real estate $34.1m; Chamber $19.8m, NAR $16.2m; AHIP $4.1m; the OBBBA was the most-lobbied bill (2,145 clients)

Citizens United, decided 21 January 2010: limits on corporate independent expenditures (2 U.S.C. 441b) invalid; Austin overruled and part of McConnell; disclaimer and disclosure upheld; independent expenditures 'do not give rise to corruption or the appearance of corruption'

Brennan Center (2025): 5-4 ruling; in 2024 more than $1bn from anonymous sources to committees supporting candidates of both parties; roughly 44% ($481m) of money raised to support Trump came from 10 donors; top 10 Harris donors nearly 8% ($126m); Musk at least $277m; Adelson over $100m

Gilens and Page (2014): 1,779 policy issues 1981-2002; average citizens have little or no independent influence; low elite support passes ~18%, high ~45%; business groups about twice the influence of mass-based groups

Bashir (2015): elite coefficient 0.76 vs median 0.03; income-group preferences correlated (r 0.78 corrected); R-squared 0.074; when median-income Americans favour change at 80%+ it happens 47% vs 52% for elites; in 185 disagreement cases median-income side wins 47%
Enns (2015): 50th and 90th percentile relative support correlated r=0.94 across 1,836 questions; 'Coincidental representation appears to be the norm'; strong partisans show larger gaps
Blanes i Vidal et al. (2012): ex-Senate staffer lobbyists see a 24% drop in generated revenue when their senator leaves office
HLOGA signed 14 Sept 2007 by George W. Bush (Senate 96-2, House 411-8): senators' cooling-off 1 to 2 years; quarterly LDA filings; bundling disclosure over $15,000

Bloomberg Tax: Intuit about $3m federal lobbying in first three quarters 2025 ($2.9m same period 2024); H&R Block $2.4m; ACTR (representing both) $270,000; July 2025 tax law gave IRS $15m to study a public-private alternative; provision to end Direct File removed; Intuit: 'regularly engages with policymakers'

AP: IRS email: 'IRS Direct File will not be available in Filing Season 2026'; accepted returns 140,803 (2024) and 296,531 (2025); Bessent: 'better alternatives', 'wasn't used very much'; average American spends about $140 a year preparing returns
Intuit FY2025 (to 31 July 2025): revenue $18.8bn; Consumer Group $4.9bn (+10%); TurboTax Live $2.0bn
